title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). S is a smooth, geometrically connected scheme of finite type over a number field k, with an embedding k into C. M is a finitely generated Tannakian category of smooth, semisimple ('iso') motives over S. T = T_{xi} is a Betti fibre functor at a complex point xi of S(C). G = Aut_⊗(T) is the motivic Galois group of M, so M ≅ Rep(G). P = Isom_⊗(T_S, T_DR) is a G_S-torsor. It carries the Gauss–Manin integrable connection and, via T_DR, a ⊗-filtration (the Hodge filtration).

This page.
(1) Fix a base point xi_0 and take T = T_{xi_0}. The connection on P^an gives a monodromy representation Gamma = pi_1(S(C), xi_0) → G(C). One requires it to factor through G(Q), which is automatic because horizontal sections come from the rational Betti local system. Call the result w.
(2) Choose a point x_0 in P(xi_0), i.e. a trivialisation of the fibre (an isomorphism T_{xi_0} → T_DR,xi_0). This gives a unique map q from the universal cover S̄_C to P^an(C) sending the marked point to x_0. It is equivariant: q(s̄γ) = q(s̄) w(γ).
(3) Hence the reduction of structure group of P^an from G(C) to G(Q): P̃_C = S̄_C ×^Gamma G(Q), embedded in P^an_C. This is the Betti rational structure, seen as a G(Q)-covering of S(C).
(4) The key new structure is a map f: P̃_C → V_G. Here V_G is the space of Hodge structures on G_R, i.e. homomorphisms h: 𝕊 = Res_{C/R} G_m → G_R compatible with a fixed weight cocharacter i: G_{m,R} → G. The conditions are:
- (a) f is holomorphic;
- (b) f is G(Q)-equivariant;
- (c) for x over s, the Hodge structure on T_C on Rep(G) defined by f(x) matches the Hodge filtration carried by P_S under the trivialisation p(x).

On the next page this becomes an equivariant map S̄_C → Y_G with f(s̄γ) = w(γ)^{-1}·f(s̄): a G-valued period map into a Mumford–Tate-type domain. A further adelic datum follows: a factorisation of Gamma → G(Q) → G(A_f) through the étale pi_1(S, xi_0). There is also a discussion of the component group G/G^0 via (P/G^0)^an.

In modern terms, Grothendieck is writing down what a family of motives with motivic Galois group G 'is' analytically and arithmetically. The data are:
- a G(Q)-local system;
- a holomorphic equivariant period map to a space of homomorphisms 𝕊 → G_R with fixed weight;
- an adelic/étale extension of the monodromy.
This is precisely the shape of the data that later defines a morphism S → Sh_K(G, X) together with its Galois/canonical-model structure (Deligne 1971/1979). The aim is to describe the 'motivic' torsor P through Hodge plus Betti plus adelic data.
errors: Condition (b) as written, f(xg) = g^{-1} f(x), is shorthand. For f valued in Hom(𝕊, G_R), G(Q) acts by inner automorphisms, so the correct formula is f(xg) = Int(g^{-1})∘f(x). The deleted passage on the previous page ('sur Y_G par autom. intérieurs') shows Grothendieck meant this.

V_G (all h: 𝕊 → G_R with given weight) is generally a disjoint union of G(R)-orbits. Its complex structure (and so 'holomorphic' in (a)) needs the embedding into flag varieties, which is not spelled out.
Griffiths transversality is not listed among the conditions. It is only implicit through (c) and the Gauss–Manin connection on P.
Condition (c) is cut off at the bottom of the page ('est compatible' continues on the next page).
On the next page, b) is written f(xg) = w(g)^{-1} f(x) 'pour s ∈ S'. It should read f(s̄γ) = w(γ)^{-1}·f(s̄), for γ ∈ Gamma, s̄ ∈ S̄_C.

ideas.what: Monodromy of the de Rham/Betti comparison torsor of a family of motives lands in G(Q), where G is the motivic Galois group; reduction of P^an to a G(Q)-local system P̃_C = S̄ ×^Gamma G(Q)
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy representation into the motivic (or Mumford–Tate) group; G-local system / Betti structure on a period torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971); André (monodromy and motivic Galois groups, 1992)

ideas.what: Hodge structures described as homomorphisms 𝕊 = Res_{C/R} G_m → G_R compatible with a fixed weight cocharacter G_m → G, applied to the motivic Galois group G
ideas.modern_name: Deligne torus description of Hodge structures; Mumford–Tate domain / space of h's
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1970–71); Mumford (1966) for the circle/Hodge-group version

ideas.what: Holomorphic G(Q)-equivariant map f from the universal cover (or the G(Q)-torsor) to V_G, compatible with the Hodge filtration of T_DR via the torsor P
ideas.modern_name: Period map of a variation of Hodge structure with G-structure (G-VHS) into a Mumford–Tate domain
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (period maps, 1968–70); Deligne (Shimura varieties, 1971/79); Green–Griffiths–Kerr (Mumford–Tate domains, 2012)

ideas.what: Adelic datum: factorisation of Gamma → G(Q) → G(A_f) through the étale fundamental group pi_1(S, xi_0) (next page), with the component group G/G^0 handled via (P/G^0)^an
ideas.modern_name: Adelic level structure and Galois action, as in canonical models of Shimura varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura; Deligne (Travaux de Shimura 1971; Variétés de Shimura 1979)

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck packages a family of motives with motivic Galois group G into exactly the triple later used for Shimura data and canonical models. The triple is: a G(Q)-local system; a holomorphic equivariant map into a space of h: 𝕊 → G_R with fixed weight; and an étale/adelic extension of the monodromy to G(A_f). This is a motivic precursor of Deligne's (G, X, K) formalism and of the 'motivic' heuristic for Shimura varieties, predating Deligne 1971 and Mumford–Tate domains.
missed.quote: Comme structure importante, il y a une application f : P̃_C → V_G où V_G est l'espace des structures de Hodge sur G_R (compatibles, i.e. liées avec un morphisme G_mR → G donné)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the Tannakian period-torsor viewpoint on Hodge/Shimura theory, including the Deligne-torus description of Hodge structures with values in a reductive group, was already in Grothendieck's motivic Galois group notes. This bears on attribution of the 'h: 𝕊 → G_R' formalism. It is also relevant to current work on period maps for G-torsors (o-minimal/definable period maps, Bakker–Brunebarbe–Tsimerman) phrased via the de Rham–Betti torsor.

missed.claim: The program sketched on pages 40–42 is to characterise families of motives over S with group G by Hodge, Betti and adelic data (w, f, adelic factorisation), i.e. a description of the 'moduli' of such motivic torsors. It is left incomplete; the component-group discussion trails off on the next page.
missed.quote: En termes de ξ_0 et Γ = π_1(S(C), ξ_0), on se donne une factorisation de Γ → G(Q) → G(A) par Γ → π_1(S, ξ_0) → G(A)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is close to the open problem of describing the image of motivic families (Hodge plus ℓ-adic compatibility) inside G-local systems with period maps, i.e. motivic versions of Shimura or period-domain moduli.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard (Deligne's Shimura-variety formalism and G-valued period maps). Seeing it written in 1965 is notable, though: Hodge structures as maps 𝕊 → G_R with a weight cocharacter, applied to the motivic Galois group, with an adelic/étale factorisation. This is an early, unpublished anticipation that is not usually credited to Grothendieck. It is not a new theorem, however.
transcription_corrections: 'i.e. y liées avec un morphisme G_mR → G donné' is likely 'i.e. liées avec un morphisme i: G_{m,R} → G donné'. The morphism is named i, as on the previous page ('un i: G_m → G fixé').
'un unique morphisme q/un rev. universel S̄_C de S_C dans P^an_C' should read 'un unique morphisme q du rev. universel S̄_C de S_C dans P^an_C = P(C), qui envoie le point marqué ξ̄_0 en x_0'.
In condition c), the symbol in 'f(x) : 𝕊 → G_R' is the Deligne torus 𝕊 (script S), not the base scheme S.
The marginal addition at the top reads 'et puis prenant T = T_{ξ_0},'.
